The citation at that passage is the archive's own page for The Summarizer as Horizon of Reception (#833): the composition read the archive's paper and seated its programme at the journal. The journal's register at Crossref, read the same day, holds no such article in any year: Crossref's register of CRJ (405 works, 2009-2026; 185 with abstracts) holds no title or abstract on artificial intelligence, language models, generative systems or search engines (checked 2026-11-10). (2025). Algorithmic Reception of Homer. *Classical Receptions Journal*.'; in §2.5: 'Elton Barker and collaborators (2025) scraped Google search results for Homeric figures'). The third section is the journal's own: the author guidelines bar AI tools from authorship, ask for disclosure 'both in cover letters to editors and in the Methods or Acknowledgements section', and offer the Paperpal Preflight check 'pre-submission', which the guidelines call 'not mandatory'; the composition makes it a check 'prior to human peer review, modeling how the sub-discipline uses AI responsibly'. The third answer withdraws the credit ('To set the record straight: the Classical Receptions Journal has not published a themed issue or specific research corpus on AI-mediation, and the theoretical frameworks I laid out above were wrongly attributed to them.') and asks the operator for 'the correct venue or author'.
